rules.description: Payroll, PCB/MTD and remuneration records of the exit year are kept seven years from the end of that year (ITA s.82(1)(a)) — longer than the EA s.61(2) register's six years after recording; the longest retention after exit. A former employee may be anonymised only after it.

references.title: Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 2–5: RM1,700 a month, RM65.38 / RM78.46 / RM98.08 a day for a six-, five- or four-day week and RM8.72 an hour, for every employer from 1 August 2025 (1 February 2025 for employers of five or more); domestic servants and apprentices are outside the Order.

rules.when: ((has(term.facts) && has(term.facts.pay_basis)) ? term.facts.pay_basis : "MONTHLY") == "MONTHLY" && term.employment_type in ["PERMANENT", "CONTRACT", "PROBATION"] && term.base_salary > 0.0 && term.base_salary < double(rules.minimum_wage.monthly)
rules.message: The monthly basic salary is below the RM1,700 minimum wage (Minimum Wages Order 2024).
rules.description: Minimum Wages Order 2024 paras 3, 5 (https://gajiminimum.mohr.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/PUA%20376.pdf, read 2026-10-07); National Wages Consultative Council Act 2011 s.23. A MONTHLY pay basis only: a weekly, daily, hourly or piece rate is a per-unit amount, checked by MINIMUM_WAGE_WEEKLY / _DAILY / _HOURLY / _PIECE; a part-timer by MINIMUM_WAGE_HOURLY_PART_TIME. A task-basis term (no basic salary) is paid by its task lines and is not refused here; domestic servants are outside the Order (para 2).

rules.when: term.employment_type == "PART_TIME" && term.base_salary > 0.0 && cel.bind(basis, ((has(term.facts) && has(term.facts.pay_basis)) ? term.facts.pay_basis : "MONTHLY"), cel.bind(week, has(term.facts.contract_hours_per_week) ? double(term.facts.contract_hours_per_week) : 0.0, basis == "MONTHLY" && week > 0.0 ? term.base_salary * 12.0 / (52.0 * week) < double(rules.minimum_wage.hourly) : basis == "WEEKLY" && week > 0.0 ? term.base_salary / week < double(rules.minimum_wage.hourly) : basis == "DAILY" && has(term.facts.normal_hours_per_day) && double(term.facts.normal_hours_per_day) > 0.0 ? term.base_salary / double(term.facts.normal_hours_per_day) < double(rules.minimum_wage.hourly) : false))
rules.message: The part-time hourly rate is below the RM8.72 minimum wage (a monthly basic × 12 ÷ 52 ÷ contract hours a week; a weekly rate ÷ contract hours a week; a daily rate ÷ normal hours a day).
rules.description: Minimum Wages Order 2024 para 5(1) (https://gajiminimum.mohr.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/PUA%20376.pdf, read 2026-10-07): RM8.72 an hour (RM1,700 × 12 ÷ 52 ÷ 45). A part-timer (Employment (Part-Time Employees) Regulations 2010) is held to the hourly rate: a MONTHLY or WEEKLY basis converted over terms.facts.contract_hours_per_week, a DAILY basis over terms.facts.normal_hours_per_day; an HOURLY rate is compared directly by MINIMUM_WAGE_HOURLY. Unrecorded hours leave the conversion unchecked.

rules.when: payslip.total_deductions - (has(payslip.lines.NOTICE_INDEMNITY) ? -payslip.lines.NOTICE_INDEMNITY : 0.0) - (employment.exit_date != "" && employment.exit_date <= period.to ? -((has(payslip.lines.LOAN_RECOVERY_AIR_TICKET) ? payslip.lines.LOAN_RECOVERY_AIR_TICKET : 0.0) + (has(payslip.lines.LOAN_RECOVERY_FESTIVE_ADVANCE) ? payslip.lines.LOAN_RECOVERY_FESTIVE_ADVANCE : 0.0) + (has(payslip.lines.AIR_TICKET_DEDUCTION) ? payslip.lines.AIR_TICKET_DEDUCTION : 0.0) + (has(payslip.lines.APPROVED_HOUSING_LOAN) ? payslip.lines.APPROVED_HOUSING_LOAN : 0.0)) : 0.0) > (has(payslip.lines.APPROVED_HOUSING_LOAN) ? 0.75 : 0.5) * payslip.gross
rules.message: The month's deductions exceed fifty per cent of the wages earned (Employment Act 1955 s.24(8)).
rules.description: Employment Act 1955 s.24(8)–(9) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf): every deduction under s.24 — including those authorised by other written law (s.24(2)(d): EPF, SOCSO, EIS, SKBBK, MTD) — is at most 50% of the wages earned in the month; not counted: the s.13(1) notice indemnity (s.24(9)(a)) and, on the final payment, amounts due to the employer and unpaid (s.24(9)(b): the advance and loan recoveries); an approved housing loan may take a further 25% (s.24(9)(c)). The slip is held for review.

rules.message: A Sabah or Sarawak worksite is outside this lineage: the Labour Ordinance (Sabah) Cap. 67 / (Sarawak) Cap. 76 governs it instead of the Employment Act, and the Ordinances are not encoded. Run the worksite on a lineage that encodes them.
rules.description: Employment Act 1955 s.1(2) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1744567_BI/Reprint%20Act%20265%20(Final).pdf): the Act extends to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan only. Labour Ordinance (Sabah) Cap. 67 as amended by Act A1753 and (Sarawak) Cap. 76 as amended by Act A1754 (in force 1 May 2025) set their own overtime, holiday, leave and termination rules; no official principal text is published, so this lineage excludes those worksites: a term recording worksite_state SABAH or SARAWAK is refused rather than priced under Employment Act rules. An unrecorded worksite is taken as Peninsular Malaysia or Labuan.

Why an employment ends (employment_contract.exit_ground, CEL employment.exit_ground): the grounds HR chooses from when it ends a contract, the employer's payroll (Infotech) list as printed. Every ground a record of this version compares is listed. `encash_annual_leave` is the default for paying untaken annual leave at exit (behaviour encash-leave-on-exit); exit_facts.annual_leave_on_exit overrides it per employee. Employment Act 1955 s.60E(3A) pays untaken annual leave on every termination except a dismissal for misconduct under s.14(1)(a), so only DISMISSAL_MISCONDUCT defaults to no encashment. Legal classes the records compare: RESIGNATION and BREACH_BY_EMPLOYEE end by the employee; BREACH_BY_EMPLOYER is the employee ending for the employer's breach (s.13(2)), as UNILATERAL is a termination by the employer; DISMISSAL and UNSATISFACTORY_PROBATION are dismissals (misconduct still by exit_facts.misconduct_dismissal), DISMISSAL_MISCONDUCT always misconduct; RETIREMENT and EMPLOYEE_RETIREMENT retire; RETRENCHMENT and RETRENCHMENT_TERM_CONTRACT retrench (replacing REDUNDANCY). Grounds list edited in place 2026-10-21 (owner: Infotech list): configuration, not law.

rules.description: C.P.8D employee remuneration file for e-Data Praisi / e-CP8D (uploaded with Form E): one pipe-delimited record per employee paid in the remuneration year, in the 22-field order of the LHDN layout Pin. 2025 (name; TIN digits; identity or passport number, 000000000000 when none; PCB category 1–3; status 1 management (employee fact organisation_management), 2 permanent or probation, 3 contract, 4 part-time, 5 industrial trainee (INTERN or the industrial_training_student fact), 6 other; retirement or contract end dd-mm-yyyy — the cessation in the year, else the signed contract end, else the Minimum Retirement Age Act 2012 s.4 age of 60 from the date of birth; tax borne by the employer 1/2 (employee fact tax_borne_by_employer); the PCB child-relief count and amount from the standing’s declared children; gross taxable remuneration as the PCB assessed base of the year’s slips (benefits in kind included); BIK_VOLA in field 11; the field-14 exempt items the catalogue carries (meal and parking allowances, child care up to RM3,000, official travel up to RM6,000, awards up to RM2,000, none for an employee who controls the employer); TP1 relief and payroll zakat as the standing’s monthly figures × months paid; EPF, PCB, CP38 and the PERKESO (SOCSO, EIS, SKBBK) employee shares). Amounts without sen are truncated (RM50,000.70 → 50000); fields 16 and 21 and the separate VOLA and ESOS fields carry no payroll record and stay blank. Named PHHHHHHHHHH_TTTT.txt from the entity’s lhdn_employer_number and the pay-date year; made only when every selected run’s pay date falls in one year. A payee (engagement PAYEE) is not an employee and is not listed.

rules.description: Children and Young Persons (Employment) Act 1966 (Act 350), reprint as at 1 December 2011 (Commissioner of Law Revision; copy read 2026-10-08 at https://ccs-co.com/wp-content/uploads/38.-Act-350-Children-and-Young-Persons-Employmen-Act-1966.pdf — jtksm.mohr.gov.my's 2019 reprint, https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/sites/default/files/2023-03/5.%20Children%20and%20Young%20Persons%20%28Employment%29%20Act%201966_0.pdf, refused the reader) ss.1A (child: not completed fifteen years; young person: not completed eighteen), 5(1)(a)–(c) and 6(1)(a)–(c): a child not between 8 pm and 7 am, not more than three consecutive hours without thirty minutes' rest, not more than six hours a day (seven with school); a young person not between 8 pm and 6 am, four consecutive hours, seven hours a day (eight with school or as an apprentice). Exceptions (public entertainment under licence; agricultural undertakings and vessels for a young person's night work) are the employer's to confirm, so this warns. The six-days-in-seven limit (s.4) is the WEEKLY_REST_DAY warning's. Peninsular Malaysia only, like this lineage. Official AGC Act A1586 (2019) read 2026-10-10: amendments do not change ss.4–6 working-time limits (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1695988_BI/06.%20A1586%20BI_unlocked.pdf).

rules.description: Children and Young Persons (Employment) Act 1966 (Act 350) s.2(2)(a)–(d) and s.2(3), as amended by Act A1586 (2019), official AGC PDF read 2026-10-10: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1695988_BI/06.%20A1586%20BI_unlocked.pdf. Checked on the term’s first day (`day`). Section 2(2A) sets minimum age thirteen for light work. Sections 2(1A)–(1B) govern Fourth Schedule hazardous work, including the supervised apprenticeship/vocational-training exception for young persons; s.2(2B) prohibits Fifth Schedule employment. Former s.2(6) was deleted. This row flags under-fifteen employment for review; CHILD_WORK_KIND, CHILD_LIGHT_WORK_AGE, MINOR_HAZARDOUS_WORK and MINOR_PROHIBITED_EMPLOYMENT enforce declared work facts. rules.when: has(employee.date_of_birth) && employee.date_of_birth != null && employee.date_of_birth != "" && age_on(employee.date_of_birth, day) < 18 && has(terms.facts.prohibited_minor_employment) && terms.facts.prohibited_minor_employment == true
rules.message: Fifth Schedule employment is prohibited for every person under eighteen (Act 350 s.2(2B)); training does not exempt it.
rules.description: Act 350 s.2 as amended by Act A1586 (2019), official AGC text read 2026-10-10: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1695988_BI/06.%20A1586%20BI_unlocked.pdf

rules.when: has(employee.date_of_birth) && employee.date_of_birth != null && employee.date_of_birth != "" && age_on(employee.date_of_birth, day) < 18 && (!has(terms.facts.hazardous_work) || !has(terms.facts.prohibited_minor_employment))
rules.message: Confirm whether this minor’s work falls under the Fourth or Fifth Schedule; unrecorded safety declarations are not proof of permitted employment.
rules.description: Act 350 s.2 as amended by Act A1586 (2019), official AGC text read 2026-10-10: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1695988_BI/06.%20A1586%20BI_unlocked.pdf

rules.when: cycle.planned.WORK != cycle.expected.WORK || cycle.planned.REST != cycle.expected.REST || cycle.planned.OFF != cycle.expected.OFF
rules.message: Swap days inside the cycle instead.
rules.description: A roster swap moves a day inside its shift pattern cycle; it never adds a work day or drops a rest or off day. Severity follows entity.validation_severity.

rules.when: run.kind in ["REGULAR", "OFF_CYCLE"]
rules.message: The jurisdiction admits regular and off-cycle payroll runs.
